D83 · the gate before any extractor decision

Is the answer key right?

Eight pages of the OPP and the SAOSO standard, each beside the grid our key says they print. One verdict per claim. Nothing here is scored — your call is the key.

8 shapes 68 claims 41 of them cells No network · autosaves on this device

Why you are being asked

The key that scores every extractor arm was written by an agent (knowledge/tests/shape_fixtures.py, commit 5c45550). Characters are already checked: every cell is proved to be a contiguous run of the committed page text. What is not checked is the grouping — whether the paper's bare row numbers are a column, whether Proud member of belongs in column 3, whether Step 3 sits inside the 1,112-character cell, and how Appendix 6a's four printed header lines become two labels.

Three independent readers (Docling, a vision model, Google's Document AI) disagree with the key on the same three or four shapes. That is either three tools failing or one unreviewed key — this page is how we find out which. The signed landscape UAT judged how the tables read; it never asked whether a cell's characters are what the paper prints.

How to judge

Open the page — the Open at full size button gives you the page at 100% so small print is legible. For each claim, answer Yes if the paper prints that, No if it does not (say what it prints instead), and Can’t tell if the scan is genuinely unreadable. Nothing is pre-filled and nothing is marked for you.

Your answers autosave in this browser. When every claim has a verdict, name, seat and date, the export button downloads one JSON file — python scripts/shape_review_signoff.py --from <that file> --dry-run turns it into a review of record, and every later change to the key is checked against it.
